headline: Opinin El Bicentenario Del Peru Que Pas Queremos Ser?

headline: Tratamiento anticancerígeno CIMAvax muestra prometedores resultados globales
content: Administered monthly since 2011 through health centers on the island, treatment has been tested in countries like Paraguay, Peru, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, and Bosnia. Today more than 5,000 patients worldwide are using active immunotherapy with CIMAvax, says Dr. Soraida Acosta, head of clinical trials department in Santiago de Cuba.  Theres no miracle The CIMAvax isnt a miraculous Cuban-developed cure but rather akin to treatments elsewhere because many scientists globally focus on activating patient immune systems for fighting cancer, explains doctoral student Nils Graber from Paris School of Social Sciences studying Cuban scientific innovation.  Immunotherapy discovered by U.S.s James P. Allison and Japan’s Tasuku Honjo recently won the Medicine Nobel Prize.  Based on unique mechanisms allowing it to starve cancer cells, according to Dr. Douglas Plessinger, Scientific Development Director at Roswell Park Cancer Institute.  Initial tests conducted on 30 American patients presented encouraging results during World Lung Cancer Congress held in Canada, though further data production remains necessary to prove efficacy, adds Plessinger.  While Fabrice André, research director at Gustave Roussy Cancer Center in France calls for caution due to insufficient significant survival differences between vaccinated versus non-vaccinated patients, he notes potential interest should medication improve and better select suitable patients.
